title: The Census Bureau Is Overrun With Staffers From a MAGA Think Tank
gist: At least seven members of the America First Policy Institute have been detailed to the US Census Bureau under the Intergovernmental Personnel Act with special sworn status granting access to sensitive data, working on a project explicitly framed around answering questions from political appointees. Two of them co-authored an anonymously published August report claiming thousands of noncitizens voted in 2020 that WIRED previously found used faulty methodology, raising concern the bureau's data could be used to contest the midterms or the 2028 election.

insights.claim: At least seven members of a single Trump-aligned think tank have been or are currently staffed at the US Census Bureau, all detailed through the Intergovernmental Personnel Act, which permits specialized personnel from nonprofits and universities to work for the government on temporary appointments of up to two years.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: A legitimate personnel-exchange statute is being used to place an ideologically aligned team inside the federal statistical system.
insights.quote: at least five other AFPI members have been or are currently staffed at the Census Bureau

insights.claim: All of the detailees appear to hold the 'special sworn status' necessary to access sensitive Census data, and are listed under a single project focused on 'ad hoc data analyses' answering questions from senior leaders at Census and the Department of Commerce.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Access plus a mandate to serve political leadership is the precise combination that statistical-agency safeguards were built to prevent.
insights.quote: All of the AFPI detailees appear to have the “special sworn status” necessary to access sensitive Census data.

insights.claim: The project appears to be led by the bureau's recently appointed deputy director for data, policy, and science, a political appointee and former fellow at the Claremont Institute.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Political appointment at the data-governance layer, not just the detailee layer, is what makes the arrangement durable.

insights.claim: A Census employee speaking anonymously said there has historically been 'nothing close' to what the think tank is doing at the bureau and called it disrespectful to the institution.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Internal staff regard the arrangement as unprecedented, which matters for assessing whether this is routine personnel exchange.
insights.quote: Frankly, it's disrespectful to the institution

insights.claim: The bureau's former associate director for research and methodology and chief scientist said having so many people from a single organization would be 'unusual.'
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: A former chief scientist confirming abnormality strengthens the case that norms, not just optics, were breached.

insights.claim: A second anonymous Census employee said data access is only allowed through approved projects where users must explain their intended use and output, and flagged that this project appears to lack civil servant involvement while explicitly referencing answering questions of interest to political appointees.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The absence of career civil servants removes the internal check that project-based data access assumes exists.
insights.quote: explicit reference to answering questions of interest to political appointees

insights.claim: A Cornell professor who studies the census argues that while agencies do bring in multiple detailees through vehicles like the American Association for the Advancement of Science, this think tank is a partisan group with an agenda rather than an institution built for independent statistical research.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
entities: American Association for the Advancement of Science
insights.so_what: The distinction is between a scientific clearinghouse and an advocacy organization, which determines whether the mechanism is being abused.
insights.quote: This is a partisan group with an agenda

insights.claim: The same scholar says supplying data to political appointees is a clear departure from the bureau's mandate, which does not include that function, and undermines the cultural norms that keep the agency transparent.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Statistical-agency independence rests on norms rather than hard law, which is why it can be eroded without any rule being broken.
insights.quote: These are all part of culture norms and practices of how you make certain you run a transparent agency

insights.claim: Neither the Census Bureau nor the think tank responded to requests for comment, and none of the named individual detailees responded either.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Blanket non-response leaves the reporting uncontested on the record.
insights.quote: The Census Bureau and AFPI did not respond to requests for comment.

insights.claim: In August the Census Bureau published an anonymously authored report titled 'Noncitizen Voting in the 2020 Election: A Beginning Analysis' claiming thousands of noncitizens voted in the 2020 election.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: An official federal statistical agency lending its imprimatur to a fraud claim is qualitatively different from a think tank publishing one.
insights.quote: Noncitizen Voting in the 2020 Election: A Beginning Analysis

insights.claim: A prior WIRED investigation found the report appeared to employ faulty methodology casting its conclusions into doubt, and identified two of its authors as employees of the right-wing think tank with deep ties to the administration.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Anonymous authorship concealed a conflict of interest that would otherwise have been visible on the report's face.

insights.claim: Experts and Census employees worry the noncitizen voting report is the first salvo in Census data possibly being used to undermine the results of the upcoming midterms or the 2028 presidential election.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The stated fear is forward-looking: the data access matters because of what it enables in future election disputes.

insights.claim: The Census Bureau holds vast troves of sensitive data on nearly every person living in the country, used for apportioning and drawing congressional districts and for allocating federal funding based on population sizes.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Census outputs determine both political representation and federal dollar flows, which is why control of the agency is contested.

insights.claim: The Department of Commerce was circulating a rule change that would eliminate noncitizens from being counted in the Census, a move that could drastically reshape how congressional districts are drawn.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Changing who counts in apportionment is a structural redistricting lever more powerful than any single election outcome.

insights.claim: Republicans have targeted differential privacy, a statistical method used to protect individual respondents' privacy, alleging it makes the Census count inaccurate in ways that favor Democrats in congressional apportionment.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: A technical privacy-preserving method has become a partisan battleground, an example of statistical infrastructure being politicized.
insights.quote: a little-known statistical method called differential privacy

insights.claim: The Census Bureau's Data Stewardship Executive Policy charter was updated in July to remove stipulations that prevented political appointees from interfering with the bureau's data.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The governing document was amended to permit exactly the kind of political access the detailee project represents.
insights.quote: had been updated in July to remove stipulations that prevented political appointees from interfering with the bureau’s data

insights.claim: In 2021, less than two weeks after the January 6 insurrection, the Census Bureau director resigned after an Inspector General letter revealed whistleblower allegations that Census workers had been pressured by political appointees to produce a report on the citizenship status of every US resident.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: There is direct precedent for the same pressure pattern, which makes the current arrangement a repeat rather than a novelty.

insights.claim: The think tank has been integral to shaping the administration's policies and makeup, with its first CEO now agriculture secretary and a former board member now education secretary.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The organization is a staffing pipeline for the executive branch, which contextualizes its placement inside a statistical agency.

insights.claim: Former staffers of the think tank occupy some of the highest ranks of the administration, including the former attorney general, the secretary of Veterans Affairs, the secretary of Housing and Urban Development, the EPA administrator, the US permanent representative to NATO, a deputy director of the White House Domestic Policy Council, and the National Economic Council director.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The breadth of placement across cabinet and economic policy roles shows the organization's institutional reach.

insights.claim: One detailee is the think tank's director for secure elections policy, a former Trump campaign staffer and election denier who was subpoenaed by the Department of Justice in 2022 in the investigation of attempts to overturn the 2020 election and was not charged.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The specific individual placed inside Census has a documented role in prior efforts to contest election results.

insights.claim: In a 2020 video posted by the Arizona Republican Party where fake electors attempted to deliver the state's electoral votes to Trump, Politico identified a man wearing a jacket with that detailee's surname passing out documents for electors to sign declaring themselves duly elected and qualified, and CNN later reported he was prepared to serve as a backup elector for the same group.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Independently reported ties to the fake elector effort sharpen the conflict-of-interest question around his data access.

insights.claim: The same detailee helped write part of an early version of the Save America Act while working for the Republican majority House Committee on House Administration, legislation that would require proof of citizenship to vote and that experts say could disenfranchise more than 20 million people.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: A 20-million-voter disenfranchisement estimate quantifies the stakes of the legislative agenda connected to the Census placement.
insights.quote: a move that experts say could disenfranchise more than 20 million people

insights.claim: Other detailees include a researcher from the think tank's Office for Fiscal and Regulatory Analysis, a program assistant who describes himself on LinkedIn as a research engineer, a research engineer with expertise in computing and machine learning, and a fellow who is an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin with an MIT economics PhD focused on tax policy.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The skill mix is data-engineering and economics heavy, consistent with a team built to run analyses on microdata.

insights.claim: One person listed as a detailee from the think tank is not listed as a staff member on its website, though an organizational email address with his name appears to exist and the group would not confirm his association.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Opaque affiliation records make it hard to audit who exactly holds sworn access to federal microdata.
